overall: The AG found the Wales ZBA violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to provide real-time public access to its June 29, 2020 remote hearing, but found no violation in admitting the applicant and counsel in person.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the ZBA failed to provide adequate, alternative means for the public to virtually attend its June 29 remote public hearing.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the ZBA violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to provide real-time access to the June 29 meeting without showing that the inability to provide real-time access to the meeting was despite best efforts and due to economic hardship.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the ZBA let non-members, an applicant and his counsel, attend the June 29 hearing in person while the general public could not.
allegations.key_passage: For this reason, we find that the ZBA did not violate the Law when it allowed an applicant and his counsel to attend the June 29 meeting in person, without permitting the general public to attend in person.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the ZBA’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the ZBA that a determination by our Office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
